title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
lede: Addy Osmani's post on the claude.dev blog explains how the Claude Code team, whose code is roughly 90% written and reviewed by Claude, makes agents prove a change works before a person looks.

points: It ranks end-to-end tests first, then property tests for edge cases and differential tests that use the old system as the oracle.
A repo-level verify skill tells Claude how to boot and drive the app, and it runs before every commit.
Checks still failing after three rounds stop the agent and call in a human.
A 39-item reliability checklist fires from the diff, and review rules are read from the base branch so a change cannot edit its own checks.
A commit gate with off, observe and enforce modes flags commits made without review or verification.

points.text: The top comment calls the approach token-hungry, arguing Playwright gives deterministic browser checks at almost no cost.
Cost recurs: one commenter already spends about $2,000 a month on one or two agents and asks how hundreds could be affordable.
Commenters split on whether every diff can still get human review if work is cut into small enough pieces.
Several want deterministic checks above the linter level, since stochastic output can only be trusted through deterministic verification.
